 Follow us on Facebook Twitter Hello Soccer MLS LaLiga World Cup Premier League Champions League CONCACAF Champions USWNT Serie A Bundesliga Ligue 1 Liga mexicana Europa League Liga MX América vs. Pumas: The $83 million roster gap behind Mexico City’s biggest rivalry
 Pumas and América head into the Capital Classic with very different realities, both in the overall table and in the value of their respective squads.
 Luis Cortes Mariano Sánchez twitter Andy Hall México Update: Nov 6th, 2026 09:39 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google The Mexico City rivalry between Pumas and Club América is about much more than bragging rights. The two historic rivals are also separated by a massive financial gap , with their combined squad valuations differing by more than $83 million , according to Transfermarkt’s market estimates for the 2026 Apertura tournament.
 América heads into Saturday’s clash with a squad valued at approximately $151.4 million , while Pumas’ roster is worth an estimated $68.4 million . That puts the difference at roughly $83 million, highlighting the contrasting financial scale of the two clubs.

 In other words, América’s squad is worth 2.21 times as much as Pumas’ . The gap isn’t simply a matter of roster size, however. The individual market values of each team’s biggest stars play a major role.
 América boasts a roster worth more than $150 million 
 The Águilas have 31 registered players , with an average age of 26.8. Thirteen are foreign players, accounting for 41.9% of the squad, while 12 have international status.
 Carlos Álvarez is América’s most valuable player , with an estimated market value of $17.3 million . The Spanish midfielder leads a list that also includes Santiago Ramos Mingo and Brian Rodríguez , both valued at $13.8 million .
 Seguimos preparándonos. 🎯 pic.twitter.com/Z1iiDyBnjI 
— Club América (@ClubAmerica) November 5, 2026 
 Santiago Bueno is next, with a valuation of $11.5 million , followed by Álex Zendejas at $10.4 million .
 Together, those five players are worth approximately $66.7 million. That’s nearly the same as the entire Pumas roster , which Transfermarkt values at $68.4 million.
 The financial advantage becomes even more apparent when looking at individual positions. América has several other players valued above $5 million, including Israel Reyes , Érick Sánchez and Raphael Veiga , each estimated to be worth $6.9 million.
 Who are Pumas’ most valuable players? 
 For Pumas , Paraguayan striker Robert Morales leads the rankings with a market value of $8.1 million. Pedro Vite follows at $7.5 million.
 Juntos por la Jornada 16 👊🐾 #SiemprePumas pic.twitter.com/DOP4EBXiJ3 
— PUMAS (@PumasMX) November 5, 2026 
 Rodrigo López ranks third at $5.2 million, while Nathan Silva, Adalberto Carrasquilla and Juninho are each valued at $4.6 million.
 Pumas have 28 players on their roster, three fewer than América. Their average age is 26.7, virtually identical to that of their city rivals.
 The makeup of the squad is also relatively similar. Pumas have 11 foreign players , representing 39.3% of the roster, along with six players classified as internationals.
 Despite those similarities in age and foreign-player representation, the biggest distinction is the market value of each team’s top performers. América has four players valued at $10 million or more. Pumas, meanwhile, don’t have a single player who reaches that threshold.
 Hoy se entrenó en el 🏟️ Olímpico Universitario ⚽️
¡Nos vemos el sábado aquí! 👋 #SiemprePumas pic.twitter.com/kMAUKzCX29 
— PUMAS (@PumasMX) November 4, 2026 
 How much more valuable are América’s top stars? 
 The gap is particularly striking when comparing the five most valuable players on each roster.
 América’s top five— Carlos Álvarez, Santiago Ramos Mingo, Brian Rodríguez, Santiago Bueno and Álex Zendejas —have a combined market value of $66.7 million.
 On the Pumas side, Robert Morales, Pedro Vite, Rodrigo López, Nathan Silva and Adalberto Carrasquilla combine for $30 million.
 That’s a difference of $36.9 million.
 Even more telling, América’s five most valuable players alone are worth 97.8% of the entire Pumas squad.
 It’s important to note that these figures are Transfermarkt ’s own market-value estimates. They are not player salaries, club budgets or guaranteed transfer fees. Actual transfer prices can vary considerably depending on contract situations, negotiations and other factors.
 Keep fighting, Águilas! 🦅 pic.twitter.com/bFV32XH6cQ 
— Club América EN (@ClubAmerica_EN) November 1, 2026 
 The Capitalino Classic comes with a Liguilla spot on the line 
 The financial comparison adds another layer of intrigue to Saturday’s matchup , which comes at a crucial point in the 2026 Apertura campaign.
 América sits at the top of the standings , while Pumas occupies 10th place . The university side needs valuable points in the closing stages of the regular season to keep its hopes of reaching the Liguilla, Mexico’s postseason championship round, alive.
 The game will take place at Estadio Olímpico Universitario, where Esteban Solari’s Pumas will look to make home-field advantage count against the Águilas.
 América may have a considerably more expensive roster on paper, but market valuations don’t win soccer games.
 The $83 million gap illustrates the difference in financial resources between two of Mexico’s biggest clubs. Once the whistle blows, however, the only numbers that matter will be on the scoreboard.
